issues.title: What is ES-level carriage for? As drafted it takes the costs of two designs and the benefits of neither
issues.author: t0ms
issues.body:
> Context: one of a set of separate follow-ups to #7, from evaluating m2ts packaging for broadcast **primary distribution / contribution handed off to hardware IRDs** (SRT/Zixi/RIST-style satellite replacement). This round is prompted by the published three-mode restructure of §5.5. Background: https://github.com/tdrapier-wbd/moq-mpegts-paper (public technical evaluation, not yet widely announced).

## The question

§5.5.3 defines a third carriage mode in which each MoQ track carries the TS packets of a single PID.
Reading it against the other two modes and against the one media-aware MoQ implementation that
exists, I cannot identify what the mode is *for* — and I think that is because as drafted it takes on
the costs of two different designs and the benefits of neither.

This is offered as a question with a recommendation, not as a defect report. If the mode has a
purpose I have missed, saying so in the document would help implementers more than any of the smaller
changes I have raised.

## What the mode costs

ES-level carriage imposes obligations that program-level carriage does not:

- **Cross-track group alignment** (§5.5.3), which is unsatisfiable literally for tracks on different
  access-unit grids (#31) — and expensive to approximate.
- **PSI reconstruction at the subscriber.** §5.5.3 and §8 require the subscriber to build a PAT and
  a PMT listing the subscribed PIDs.
- **A timing reference that lives in another track.** §6.7: a subscriber requiring PCR-based timing
  MUST subscribe to the track where `m2tsPcrPid` equals `m2tsEsPid`, so the tracks are not
  independent and a partial subscription may be untimeable.
- **Re-interleaving N independent streams into one multiplex** that still has to satisfy the T-STD,
  with no declared mux rate available — §6.9 forbids `m2tsMuxRate` in this mode (#25).
- **A loss of descriptor context.** The originating PMT's descriptors — language, AC-3, teletext,
  component — are what a broadcast receiver uses to identify components. A subscriber constructing a
  PMT from scratch has no instruction to carry them forward, and §5.5.3 only says publishers SHOULD
  put the original PAT and PMT in `initDataList`. What the subscriber does with the descriptors in
  that PMT when building its own is unstated. *(This one is a straightforward omission and I am happy
  to raise it separately if the mode is retained in its current form.)*

## What it buys

Selective component subscription: take the video and one audio, drop the second language, drop the
EPG. That is genuinely useful, and for a client with constrained bandwidth it is the point.

What it does not buy is anything media-aware. The payload is still transport-stream packets, so:

- Group boundaries are placed by the publisher's packet-level policy, not by access-unit structure,
  unless the publisher demuxes enough to find random access points — at which point it is doing the
  work of mode 3-as-access-units without the benefit.
- Objects are packet-count-sized rather than frame-sized, so per-frame priority and per-frame
  shedding are not available.
- Codec configuration is inside the elementary stream, so a subscriber must parse transport-stream
  and PES syntax before it can initialise a decoder — the catalog tells it a PID and a role, not a
  codec configuration.

So the mode sits between program-level carriage, which is simple and has a clear purpose, and
access-unit carriage, which is complex and gets something for the complexity.

## What the one implementation does instead

`moq-dev/moq`'s media-aware lane — the implementation this mode most resembles at a glance — does
not do this. Its per-elementary-stream tracks carry **decoded access units** for codecs it
understands and reassembled PES payloads for those it does not; continuity counters, PAT, PMT and PCR
are discarded on ingest and regenerated at egress; and the catalog carries codec configuration and
the service information tables directly. Group boundaries fall at keyframes for video and at frame
boundaries for audio.

That is a fourth mode, not an instance of §5.5.3, and it is the one that yields the media-aware
properties: joins land on a random access point by construction rather than by scanning, objects are
frame-sized, and a subscriber initialises from the catalog. Its price is that the egress must
reconstruct the transport stream, including its timing — which is the subject of the output-timing
issue and is a real cost, not a free lunch.

## Recommendation

Resolve the mode toward one neighbour or the other.

**Either** pull it back and present it honestly as **selective component subscription** — which means
saying so in §5.5.3, dropping or weakening the cross-track alignment MUST, and accepting that a
subscriber recombining tracks is doing a best-effort re-multiplex rather than producing a
broadcast-grade output. This is the small change and it makes the mode coherent.

**Or** push it forward to **access-unit carriage**, which means specifying what an access-unit track
carries, how codec configuration reaches the catalog, and — necessarily — what the egress must do to
produce a conformant transport stream from it. This is the larger change, it is the mode with the
most implementation experience behind it, and it is the one that justifies the complexity the section
already imposes.

I have a preference for the second, on the grounds that the complexity is already in the section and
the benefit is not. But the first is a perfectly defensible scoping decision, and either is better
than the present position, where the costs of the second are charged for the benefits of the first.

---

issues.title: TR 101 290 P1 does not detect the failure mode that regenerated m2ts carriage produces
issues.author: t0ms
issues.body:
> Context: one of a set of separate follow-ups to #7, from evaluating m2ts packaging for broadcast **primary distribution / contribution handed off to hardware IRDs** (SRT/Zixi/RIST-style satellite replacement). This round is prompted by the published three-mode restructure of §5.5. Background: https://github.com/tdrapier-wbd/moq-mpegts-paper (public technical evaluation, not yet widely announced).

## What this is not asking for

Not a reporting mechanism, not a schema, and not a control plane. Subscriber health reporting applies
identically to LOC, CMAF and `m2ts` packaging, and work on it is further advanced elsewhere; a
convention defined inside one packaging extension would fragment it. §4's list of what this document
does not define is one of its better-kept disciplines and I am not asking to breach it.

What is `m2ts`-specific — and cannot be written anywhere else — is **which measurements mean
anything for a transport stream, and which of the obvious ones do not.**

## The finding

For broadcast delivery the standard health instrument is ETSI TR 101 290 Priority 1: TS sync loss,
sync byte error, PAT error, continuity count error, PMT error, PID error. It is what monitoring
systems implement and what an operator will reach for first.

**For m2ts carriage that has been demuxed and re-multiplexed, the P1 set does not detect the failure
mode this carriage actually produces**, because the egress regenerates exactly the syntax P1
inspects. Two measurements, on one media-aware MoQ implementation:

**Programme content can stop while every P1 counter stays clean.** Suppressing one elementary stream
for 60.02 s produced a **57.22 s** hole in delivered video at the far end of the chain, with **0
continuity errors**, **0 PCR intervals above 40 ms**, and a worst PCR interval of 30.080 ms —
*identical to the control run*. The multiplex was structurally perfect throughout and carried no
picture. *(File domain, loopback, groomed chain, `moq 0.10.0` / relay `0.14.15`.)*

**A live defect presents the same way, permanently.** An open regression in that implementation
stalls video and the primary audio on a content join, while PSI, AC-3 and teletext keep flowing.
Measured: **0.31 Mb/s** delivered against a 9.0–9.8 Mb/s parent, sustained with no recovery across
40 minutes and 235 samples, and not cleared by 80 further subscriber joins. A receiver locks. A
monitor asking "is the multiplex present, and is it syntactically clean" reports health.

The general form: this carriage separates the *structure* of a transport stream from its *content*,
and then rebuilds the structure. P1 measures the structure. So the metric most likely to be deployed
is the one least able to see the characteristic fault — which is the opposite of the situation in a
conventional contribution chain, where a fault damages structure and content together and P1 is a
good proxy.

What does detect it is **per-PID access-unit rate**: counting access units per elementary stream
against an expected cadence. That is a measurement of content, it requires parsing beyond P1's scope,
and it is not in any standard monitoring profile.

## Proposed change

One paragraph, as an Implementation Considerations note or as an addition to §8:

> Health assessment of an m2ts track requires observation of elementary-stream content in addition to
> the transport-stream error indicators of ETSI TR 101 290. Where a publisher or subscriber
> reconstructs Program Specific Information, continuity counters or the Program Clock Reference
> rather than carrying them unmodified, those indicators describe the reconstruction and not the
> carried content: an elementary stream may cease while continuity counters remain sequential and PCR
> repetition remains within limits. Implementations monitoring such a track SHOULD additionally
> observe the presence and rate of access units per elementary stream. The mechanism by which such
> observations are reported is outside the scope of this document.

The conditional framing matters: the paragraph is scoped to modes where the syntax is regenerated,
which is where the problem exists. Unmodified carriage keeps the source's counters and PCR intervals,
so P1 remains a reasonable proxy there — and saying so is part of the value, because it tells an
implementer which mode choice changes their monitoring obligations.

---

comments.author: gwendalsimon
comments.body:
Not taking this one for now. Your measurement comes from a lane that regenerates PSI, continuity counters and PCR, which you note is a fourth mode rather than an instance of §5.5.3. Modified carriage here passes the elementary-stream packets through with their original counters and PCR, so a stopped stream stops arriving and P1 PID error fires.

Reopen if that reasoning is wrong for one of the modes as drafted.

comments.body: Your reasoning holds for the modes as drafted — modified carriage passes the elementary-stream packets through with their original counters and PCR, so a stopped stream stops arriving and P1 fires. Our lane regenerates all three, which is not a mode this document defines. Closing.

Follows draft-ietf-moq-cmsf as structural template. One deliberate deviation from CMSF: abstract uses "extends" (not "updates") to avoid the IETF Updates boilerplate implication.

  * Remove unused references — JSON, LANG, MIME (normative), HLS (informative). None cited in body.

pulls.title: add Multi-Program Transport Stream (MPTS) handling
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
The current draft is silent on MPTS sources. This PR establishes the one-track-per-program model with clear PAT rewriting and CA scoping rules. Scrambled-stream CA handling is deferred to the content-protection PR.
 
- Adds `single-program transport stream` and `multi-program transport stream` defined terms to Definitions
- Adds normative `## Multi-Program Source Handling` subsection: one-track-per-program model, PAT rewriting, PMT/PCR/ES packet retention, null packet handling, CA scoping for scrambled sources, and `altGroup` guidance
- Tightens `m2tsProgramNumber` from a decoder hint to a program identity declaration, with back-reference to the new section
- Fixes `m2tsPcrPid` definition for consistency with `m2tsPmtPid`
- Adds a non-normative catalog example: two tracks derived from a single 2-program MPTS source

pulls.title: Group start semantics, PSI bootstrapping, and join behavior
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
Group Numbering: replace vague "random access boundaries" with an explicit self-containment criterion — IDR always valid; CRA valid only when its RASL pictures don't reference frames from a prior Group; publishers not required to start a new Group at every intra point

Switching: strengthen altGroup Group-boundary alignment — video tracks MUST place boundaries at identical positions; other tracks SHOULD align where possible

Object Boundaries: replace "decoder initialization" with explicit separation of PAT/PMT (transport-level, required) from codec-level init (in elementary stream, present at any RAP)

Initialization Data: add publisher SHOULD to update initData when PSI changes in a live track

Subscriber Processing: add m2tsPsiInterval-bounded look-back SHOULD; MAY use MSF Media Timeline for Joining FETCH resolution; MUST NOT present before valid PAT+PMT received

Relay Processing: replace unverifiable "contains PSI data" retention condition with observable m2tsRandomAccess flag

pulls.author: gwendalsimon

    - MUST NOT introduce PCR discontinuity within a MOQT Group

    - PCR wrap-around is a normal event; references MSF Media Timeline as an alternative monotonic abstraction

pulls.title: feat: add m2tsMpts transparent whole-multiplex carriage mode
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses point 3 of #7 — the request for an explicit transparent profile for whole-multiplex carriage.

- Defines a new boolean catalog field `m2tsMpts` that, when true, signals that the track carries the full multi-program transport stream without program selection, PID filtering, or PAT rewrite
- Names the field after its content rather than publisher behavior, distinguishing it from per-program transparent forwarding of a SPTS
- Propagates the constraint and semantics across all affected sections of the draft

## Changes

**§5.2 Object Boundaries** — scopes the "Group starts with PAT and PMT" guidance to single-program video tracks

**§5.5 Multi-Program Source Handling** — adds two paragraphs defining the `m2tsMpts` mode; Group boundaries use a fixed Object count unless the publisher can identify RAPs and sets `m2tsRandomAccess`

**Catalog table and field definitions**
- New `m2tsMpts` entry and section
- `m2tsProgramNumber`, `m2tsPmtPid`, `m2tsPcrPid`: each gains a MUST-be-absent clause when `m2tsMpts` is true
- `m2tsPsiInterval`: distinguished between normative SHOULD (single-program) and advisory (MPTS)
- `initData`: closing paragraph noting that MPTS requires extracting PAT and all program PMTs

**§7 Examples** — rename per-program example to avoid confusion; add Transparent MPTS Carriage example

**§8 Subscriber Processing** — clarify "PMT for the track" to "PMT for the program to be decoded"

**§10 Switching** — add MUST NOT prohibiting `m2tsMpts` tracks from `altGroup`

pulls.title: refactor: remove relay processing section
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

MOQT relays forward and cache Objects based on MOQT-layer metadata: namespace, track, Group ID, Object ID, and delivery metadata.  They have no mechanism to read MSF catalog fields, which are application-layer information exchanged between publishers and subscribers outside the relay's scope.

The removed section conditioned relay cache behavior on `m2tsRandomAccess`, an MSF catalog field.  Because a relay cannot read catalog fields, this guidance was unenforceable and incorrect.  The remaining text — that relays are not required to parse MPEG-2 Transport Stream syntax and may discard Groups per MOQT cache policy — is already implied by MOQT being payload-agnostic and adds no m2ts-specific normative content.

Relay behavior for m2ts tracks is fully governed by the base MOQT specification; no m2ts-specific relay section is needed.

pulls.title: feat: add m2tsMuxRate field and null-packet CBR warning
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses point 2 of #7 — null packet removal breaks CBR byte-clock and mux-clock recovery.

Point 2 notes that §5.5 permits null packet removal at publisher discretion, but removing null packets changes the byte distance between successive PCRs.  Constant-bit-rate receivers use that spacing to reconstruct the mux clock; without it, a downstream device must re-derive a rate it was never told.  The issue suggested either recommending that nulls be retained for CBR reconstruction, or defining an advisory catalog field for the source mux rate.

This PR implements the catalog field option.

## Changes

**§5.5 Multi-Program Source Handling** — adds a paragraph warning that removing null packets changes the inter-packet byte spacing that constant-bit-rate receivers use to recover the mux clock, and that publishers removing null packets SHOULD declare `m2tsMuxRate`.

**Catalog table** — new `m2tsMuxRate` entry.

**New field `m2tsMuxRate`** — optional advisory Number (bits/s).  A subscriber reconstructing a constant-bit-rate output stream MAY use this value to restore the original mux rate when null packets have been removed.

pulls.title: feat: add m2tsSiPids field and SI table retention guidance
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses point 1 of #7 — the §5.5 retain filter silently drops DVB and ATSC service information tables.

Point 1 observes that the PMT-centric retain list in §5.5 does not include SI tables carried on fixed well-known PIDs: SDT/BAT (0x0011), EIT (0x0012), TDT/TOT (0x0014), and NIT (0x0010), or their ATSC PSIP equivalents.  A publisher implementing §5.5 without additional care produces a track with no service identity, no EPG, and no broadcast time — a disqualifier for IRD-based deployments.  The issue suggested either a normative note or a catalog hint for retained SI PIDs.

This PR implements both.

## Changes

**§5.5 Multi-Program Source Handling** — adds a paragraph noting that the PMT-centric filter silently drops DVB and ATSC SI tables, listing the affected PIDs, and stating that publishers targeting broadcast or IRD deployments SHOULD retain the required SI tables and SHOULD declare the retained PIDs using `m2tsSiPids`.

**Catalog table** — new `m2tsSiPids` entry.

**New field `m2tsSiPids`** — optional advisory Array of packet identifiers retained in the filtered track beyond those listed in the Program Map Table.  Subscribers MAY use this list to verify which service information tables are present without inspecting the packet stream.

pulls.title: feat: add CC/PID preservation MUST NOTs and PCR timing note
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

Two related clarifications for contribution and IRD deployments, addressing fidelity concerns raised in #7.

**§5.2 — continuity counter and PID preservation**

The existing text describes continuity counters, PIDs, and other transport-stream syntax as "remaining inside the source packets" — a description of what is carried, not a prohibition on modification.  A publisher forwarding a source transport stream could technically rewrite continuity counters or remap PIDs while complying with the current text.  Both modifications are silent disqualifiers for IRD receivers: a broken continuity counter sequence triggers decoder errors; PID remapping breaks demultiplexing and conditional access without warning.  This PR adds explicit MUST NOTs to match the byte-faithful carriage requirement described in #7.

**§5.5 — PCR arrival timing**

The PCR and Timing section correctly handles PCR value continuity and discontinuity signaling but says nothing about inter-packet timing.  Hardware IRDs derive the mux clock from the rate at which PCR-bearing packets arrive, not only from their encoded values.  MOQT does not guarantee that Object delivery preserves inter-packet timing; packets arrive in bursts shaped by QUIC rather than at source mux rate.  A non-normative note acknowledges this constraint, addressing the second option raised in point 4 of #7 — a statement that PCR is authoritative and that the egress should pace to it.

## Changes

**§5.2 Object Boundaries** — add MUST NOT modify continuity counters and MUST NOT remap PIDs when forwarding a source transport stream.

**§5.5 PCR and Timing** — add non-normative note on inter-packet PCR timing and IRD mux-clock recovery.

pulls.title: feat: add verbatim single-program (SPTS) carriage mode
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Problem

The draft's `Multi-Program Source Handling` section presents a single-program track only as the output of filtering an MPTS source. There is no path for a publisher that receives a native single-program transport stream and wants to carry it unchanged. Applying the filter rules to a native SPTS is unnecessary and potentially harmful: no PAT rewrite is needed (the PAT already lists one program), and the rules would inappropriately guide publishers to strip SI tables that are already correctly scoped.

This is raised in issue #14.

## Changes

- Insert a paragraph in §5.5 establishing that a publisher with a native SPTS source MAY carry it without filtering. No PAT rewrite is required; null packets and SI tables MAY be retained; per-program catalog fields SHOULD be present.
- Narrow the existing filter rules intro from "a publisher producing per-program tracks" to "a publisher deriving per-program tracks from an MPTS source", making clear those rules apply only to MPTS derivation.

No new fields. No changes to `m2tsMpts` semantics. No impact on subscriber processing or switching sections.

Closes #14.

pulls.title: fix: rewrite SI table filtering guidance and add rewrite requirement
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Problem

The SI table paragraph added in PR #11 had two gaps:

1. **Style:** The paragraph used "PMT-centric" as a label for the filter rule, referenced "the retain list above," used "well-known" informally, and bundled two SHOULD obligations into one sentence.

2. **Substance:** No guidance existed on rewriting SI tables when filtering from an MPTS. A retained SDT or EIT carried verbatim from an MPTS still advertises all programs in the multiplex, which is non-conformant for a derived single-program track.

This is raised in issue #13.

## Changes

- Rewrite the SI paragraph: start from the PMT's actual scope (elementary stream and PCR PIDs only), introduce all acronyms with full names on first use, and explain clearly why the filter drops SI tables.
- Split the two SHOULD obligations (retain SI, declare via `m2tsSiPids`) into separate sentences.
- Add rewrite guidance: because SDT and EIT from an MPTS describe all programs, publishers SHOULD filter or rewrite them to include only entries for the carried program. NIT and TDT/TOT are broadcast-wide and do not require per-program rewriting.

Closes #13.

Adds the required `m2tsModified` field and restructures source handling into two carriage modes.

pulls.title: feat(catalog): add m2tsEsPid field and ES-level carriage mode
pulls.author: gwendalsimon
pulls.body:
## Summary

Introduces ES-level carriage as a third carriage mode alongside the existing unmodified and modified modes. When `m2tsEsPid` is present, a track carries exactly one elementary stream or signaling table, enabling subscribers to select and recombine individual streams independently.

* **New `m2tsEsPid` field** (Optional, Number): identifies the single PID in the track. Requires `m2tsModified: true`. Forbids `m2tsMpts`, `m2tsPmtPid`, `m2tsSiPids`, and `m2tsScte35Pid` on the same track.
* **New §5.5.3 Modified ES-Level Carriage**: specifies track payload rules (only packets for `m2tsEsPid`; no PAT, PMT, or null packets), PCR cross-track reference semantics, Group boundary synchronization requirement across ES-level tracks for the same program, subscriber recombination obligations (construct PAT+PMT, interleave packets, source PCR from PCR-bearing track), and `altGroup` semantics for alternate audio renditions.
* **MSF `role` values defined** for SI-table and SCTE-35 tracks: `"nit"`, `"sdt"`, `"eit"`, `"tdt"`, `"scte35"`.
* **§5.5 intro updated** to describe three modes instead of two.
* **Field definitions updated**: `m2tsPmtPid`, `m2tsPcrPid`, `m2tsSiPids`, `m2tsScte35Pid` each carry new constraints and explanations specific to ES-level tracks.
* **§8 Subscriber Processing updated**: adds Group alignment and recombination requirements for ES-level subscribers.
* **New catalog example**: four-track program (video, audio-en, audio-es, EIT) illustrating the ES-level pattern.

pulls.body:
An editorial pass over the whole draft, followed by the review issues raised on 17 September.

The packaging value and every catalog field move from `m2ts` to `mpeg2ts` (to prevent conflict with M2TS, the 192-octet source packet format).

Three fields are gone: `mpeg2tsPacketsPerObject`, `mpeg2tsPmtPid`, and `mpeg2tsPsiInterval`. Each was optional and advisory, and no rule consumed any of them. Subscriber Processing and Authorization are gone too, their surviving rules moved to the sections defining their subjects.

New normative material answers the review: an Egress Timing section, a carriage mode decision table, conditional access in per-program filtering, the delivery schedule that transport stream semantics include, and the BDAV encoding of the 192-octet prefix.

Seven missing references are now cited.
